newsitem.title: UK: UK regional rail dispute widened to five new firms.
newsitem.headline: UK regional rail dispute widened to five new firms.

text.p: Britain's Rail, Maritime and Transport (RMT) union said on Thursday that its members at five regional railway companies had voted to strike over working arrangements and breaks.

RMT leader Jimmy Knapp told a news conference during the Trades Union Congress conference that the companies affected were Anglia Railway, Cardiff Railway Company, Gatwick Express ,, West Coast Mainline and Southwest Trains .
Scotrail overnight staff on Intercity sleeper trains have also voted to join other Scotrail RMT members already involved in the dispute, which has led to several one-day stoppages.
RMT members at five of the above companies -- the overnight Scotrail staff are excluded -- will hold a one-day strike on Friday September 20.

On Monday September 23, the same five companies, plus Scotrail -- both day and night services -- will be disrupted by another one-day strike, along with Regional Railways Northeast, Regional Railways Northwest and South Wales and West, already affected by previous stoppages.
Knapp said the dispute involved working practices and "physical needs breaks" -- a demand for a break of 30 minutes during the working day. --London Newsroom, +44 0171 542 7717
